subject: [RFC PATCH 6/7] memcg: remove synchronous memory.high enforcement

2026-11-22.patch_summary: This patch removes synchronous enforcement of the memory.high limit in the Linux kernel's memcg (memory cgroup) subsystem. The synchronous step, introduced to prevent priority inversion, can block tasks for up to 2 seconds and is particularly problematic for operations like mlock() that hold locks while charging a large range. The patch instead relies on the asynchronous reclaim process to handle overages when tasks return to userspace, ensuring that memory.max still limits task growth. This change aims to improve system responsiveness and reduce lock contention.
